not_tested_here: receipt-time native chat from a real network client (this lab has no attached player client)
webhook entry and the context_id it would carry (external CLI entry was used instead)
any Harness model backend; the task entry and the live mc_player calls are the whole path
ROM/fixture-level behaviour; the scene is a generic machine target, not the meta15 fixture
findings: The released mod's PLAYER reply puts the entity record under player and the ray under a separate top-level view; bridge 0.4.0 returned only player, dropping the view.
bridge 0.4.1 merges the ray into player.view; the raw mod reply stays the comparison authority.
A Carpet fake player's execute-as-say broadcast produces a context bundle with timing=broadcast, not timing=receipt; the bundle id is real and fetchable, but it is not packet-time history.
The fake players are live ServerPlayers: state.playerList includes both, and a UUID query returns that player even when another player is first in the list.
